channel.title: casualdata daily
channel.description: casualdata publishes one new interactive data visualization every day: a chart, map or picture of the day's news and data, each on its own dated page with its sources. It also keeps casualdata's data visualization art projects from 2007 to 2011.

item.title: Every forecast miss went the same way
item.description: All 435 House seats of the 2026 midterms, placed by how forecasters rated them before the election and shaded by who won: Democrats took 21 seats rated Republican and every toss-up, and Republicans took none rated Democratic.

item.title: 99 votes may decide a seat in Congress
item.description: The five closest races of the 2026 midterms, drawn as crowds side by side: one figure for every vote of the lead.

item.title: Voters split by issue, not by party
item.description: Every 2026 ballot measure on a party issue, grouped by issue, against how the same state voted for president. Abortion rights ran ahead of Democrats everywhere; transgender limits ran ahead of Republicans everywhere.

item.title: If the country were 100 people, 51 of them stayed home
item.description: The 2026 midterm electorate as a town of 100 people: who voted, for which party, and who stayed home.

item.title: Nearly every Senate race moved toward the Democrats
item.description: Each 2026 Senate race against the same state's 2024 vote for president. 30 of 31 moved toward the Democrats. The exception was Maine.

item.title: Where the light goes in November
item.description: Hours of daylight for every latitude, every day of the year. Point anywhere to read it.
